t: This is the Roderic Hill Building, a university aeronautics building in London. It's named after Air Chief Marshal Sir Roderic Hill, who lived from 1894 to 1954 and was a senior Royal Air Force commander during the Second World War. He later became Rector of Imperial College and Vice-Chancellor of London University. The building is where Imperial College's Department of Aeronautics was situated, so an airman who led the college gives his name to the place where flight was studied.
